items.q: 1 mol of an ideal gas is held at 150 kPa and 350 K. Calculate its volume in m3, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
A gas has a molar heat capacity at constant pressure of 37.1 J/(mol K). Taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K), calculate its molar heat capacity at constant volume in J/(mol K).
For a gas Cp = 37.1 J/(mol K) and Cv = 20.8 J/(mol K). Calculate the heat capacity ratio.
A reservoir at 350 K supplies 8000 J of heat reversibly. Calculate the entropy change of the reservoir in J/K.
Calculate the heat needed to raise 5 kg of a liquid of specific heat 2.4 kJ/(kg K) through 60 K, in kJ.
items.s: Q = m Cp dT = 5 x 2.4 x 60 = 720 kJ.

items.q: How much heat in kJ is needed to melt 10 kg of a solid whose latent heat of fusion is 335 kJ/kg at its melting point?
items.s: Q = m x latent heat = 10 x 335 = 3350 kJ.

items.q: A gas mixture at a total pressure of 400 kPa contains a component of mole fraction 0.2. Calculate the partial pressure of that component in kPa.
2 mol of an ideal gas fills 1.0 m3 at 400 K. Calculate its pressure in kPa, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
A vapour of molar mass 58 g/mol is held at 150 kPa and 350 K. Treating it as ideal, calculate its density in kg/m3, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
1 mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly from 1 m3 to 10 m3 at 350 K. Calculate the work done by the gas in kJ, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
A gas of heat capacity ratio 1.4 is compressed reversibly and adiabatically from 360 K, its volume falling to a quarter of the original. Calculate the final temperature in K.

One mole of a gas of heat capacity ratio 1.3 is compressed adiabatically from 300 K to an eighth of its original volume. Taking Cv = R/(gamma - 1) with R = 8.314 J/(mol K), calculate the work input in kJ.
A heat engine operates between a hot reservoir at 800 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K. Calculate its Carnot efficiency in percent.
A reversible engine working between 800 K and 320 K receives 500 kJ from the hot reservoir. Calculate the work output in kJ.
A refrigerator keeps its cold space at 270 K while rejecting heat at 310 K. Calculate its Carnot coefficient of performance.
A heat pump delivers heat at 320 K while drawing from a source at 280 K. Calculate its Carnot coefficient of performance.
1 mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly to 2 times its original volume. Calculate the change in entropy in J/K, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
items.s: dS = nR ln(V2/V1) = 1 x 8.314 x ln 2 = 5.76 J/K.

items.q: 2 mol of gas with Cp = 33.6 J/(mol K) is heated from 300 K to 450 K while its pressure rises 3.0 times. Calculate the entropy change in J/K, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
For a reaction dH = 60 kJ/mol and dS = -150 J/(mol K). Calculate dG at 400 K in kJ/mol.
The standard Gibbs free energy change of a reaction is -5 kJ/mol at 400 K. Calculate the equilibrium constant, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
A reaction has an enthalpy change of 60 kJ/mol and an equilibrium constant of 10.0 at 320 K. Use the van't Hoff relation to calculate the equilibrium constant at 350 K, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
A liquid has an enthalpy of vaporisation of 30 kJ/mol and a vapour pressure of 10 kPa at 350 K. Estimate its vapour pressure in kPa at 360 K, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).

The vapour pressure of a liquid follows the Antoine relation log10 P = A - B/(T + C) with A = 7.85, B = 1600 and C = 232 where P is in mmHg and T in degrees Celsius. Calculate P in mmHg at 60 degrees Celsius.
A liquid boils at 380 K. Using Trouton's rule that the molar enthalpy of vaporisation is about 88 J/(mol K) times the normal boiling temperature, estimate it in kJ/mol.
items.s: dHvap = 88 x Tb = 88 x 380 = 33440 J/mol = 33.44 kJ/mol.

items.q: For a reaction the standard enthalpy of formation of the product is -286 kJ/mol and that of the reactant is -226 kJ/mol. Calculate the standard heat of reaction in kJ/mol.
items.s: dHr = sum dHf(products) - sum dHf(reactants) = -286 - (-226) = -60 kJ/mol.

items.q: A gas of Joule-Thomson coefficient 0.25 K/bar is throttled through a pressure drop of 50 bar. Calculate the temperature change in K.
10 mol of a real gas occupies 0.01 m3 at 2000 kPa and 300 K. Calculate its compressibility factor, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
At a certain temperature the Henry constant of a gas in water is 4000 kPa and its partial pressure above the liquid is 20 kPa. Calculate the mole fraction dissolved, using p = H x.
An ideal liquid mixture contains a component of mole fraction 0.7 with vapour pressure 80 kPa, the remainder having vapour pressure 20 kPa. Calculate the bubble pressure of the mixture in kPa.
items.s: P = x1 P1sat + x2 P2sat = 0.7 x 80 + 0.3 x 20 = 62 kPa.

items.q: Two components have a relative volatility of 2 and the liquid mole fraction of the more volatile one is 0.4. Calculate its mole fraction in the equilibrium vapour, using y = alpha x/(1 + (alpha - 1)x).
A system has 3 components and 2 phases present in equilibrium. Calculate its number of degrees of freedom from the phase rule.
2 mol of an ideal mixture is formed from two components with mole fractions 0.4 and 0.6. Calculate the entropy of mixing in J/K, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
An ideal gas mixture contains a component of mole fraction 0.3 with molar mass 28 g/mol, the balance having molar mass 58 g/mol. Calculate the mean molar mass of the mixture in g/mol.
items.s: M = sum y_i M_i = 0.3 x 28 + 0.7 x 58 = 49 g/mol.

items.q: A compressor takes gas at 300 K and would deliver it at 500 K if the compression were isentropic. With an isentropic efficiency of 0.8, calculate the actual delivery temperature in K.
An ideal Brayton cycle operates with a pressure ratio of 4 and a working gas of heat capacity ratio 1.33. Calculate its thermal efficiency in percent.

In a steam cycle steam enters the turbine at 3200 kJ/kg and leaves at 2500 kJ/kg, the pump work is 25 kJ/kg and the heat supplied in the boiler is 2600 kJ/kg. Calculate the cycle efficiency in percent.

1 mol of an ideal gas is held at 200 kPa and 273 K. Calculate its volume in m3, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
For a gas Cp = 29.1 J/(mol K) and Cv = 25.3 J/(mol K). Calculate the heat capacity ratio.
A reservoir at 400 K supplies 8000 J of heat reversibly. Calculate the entropy change of the reservoir in J/K.
Calculate the heat needed to raise 8 kg of a liquid of specific heat 4.18 kJ/(kg K) through 80 K, in kJ.
items.s: Q = m Cp dT = 8 x 4.18 x 80 = 2675 kJ.

items.q: How much heat in kJ is needed to melt 2 kg of a solid whose latent heat of fusion is 200 kJ/kg at its melting point?
items.s: Q = m x latent heat = 2 x 200 = 400 kJ.

2 mol of an ideal gas fills 0.5 m3 at 300 K. Calculate its pressure in kPa, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).

3 mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly from 1 m3 to 10 m3 at 350 K. Calculate the work done by the gas in kJ, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
A gas of heat capacity ratio 1.3 is compressed reversibly and adiabatically from 330 K, its volume falling to half of the original. Calculate the final temperature in K.
One mole of a gas of heat capacity ratio 1.4 is compressed adiabatically from 350 K to half of its original volume. Taking Cv = R/(gamma - 1) with R = 8.314 J/(mol K), calculate the work input in kJ.
A heat engine operates between a hot reservoir at 750 K and a cold reservoir at 350 K. Calculate its Carnot efficiency in percent.
A reversible engine working between 500 K and 320 K receives 250 kJ from the hot reservoir. Calculate the work output in kJ.
A refrigerator keeps its cold space at 260 K while rejecting heat at 310 K. Calculate its Carnot coefficient of performance.
A heat pump delivers heat at 310 K while drawing from a source at 270 K. Calculate its Carnot coefficient of performance.
3 mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly to 10 times its original volume. Calculate the change in entropy in J/K, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
1 mol of gas with Cp = 33.6 J/(mol K) is heated from 320 K to 400 K while its pressure rises 3.0 times. Calculate the entropy change in J/K, taking R = 8.314 J/(mol K).
For a reaction dH = -50 kJ/mol and dS = 120 J/(mol K). Calculate dG at 500 K in kJ/mol.

For a reaction the standard enthalpy of formation of the product is -286 kJ/mol and that of the reactant is -110 kJ/mol. Calculate the standard heat of reaction in kJ/mol.
items.s: dHr = sum dHf(products) - sum dHf(reactants) = -286 - (-110) = -176 kJ/mol.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Entropy.
o: the ratio of the actual volume of a gas to the volume it would occupy if it behaved perfectly
a measure of the dispersal of energy in a body of matter, which always rises for an isolated change
a mixture that boils at constant composition because its vapour has the same composition as its liquid
the ratio of the cooling or warming effect produced to the work input of a device
items.s: Entropy: a measure of the dispersal of energy in a body of matter, which always rises for an isolated change. The other options describe Compressibility factor, Azeotrope, Coefficient of performance.

items.q: Reversible process may be defined as
o: an idealised change carried out so slowly that the material stays infinitesimally close to equilibrium
a cooling sequence in which a fluid is compressed, condensed, throttled and evaporated
a condensed phase held at a pressure above the value at which it would begin to boil
the ratio of the vapour pressures of two components, which measures how easily they can be separated
items.s: Reversible process: an idealised change carried out so slowly that the material stays infinitesimally close to equilibrium. The other options describe Compressed liquid, Relative volatility, Vapour compression refrigeration.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Standard heat of reaction.
o: the principle that the total dispersal of energy in an isolated arrangement can never decrease
the enthalpy change when reactants and products are all in their defined reference states at a stated temperature
a change carried out while the temperature of the material is held constant
the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is made from its elements in their standard states
items.s: Standard heat of reaction: the enthalpy change when reactants and products are all in their defined reference states at a stated temperature. The other options describe Heat of formation, Isothermal process, Second law of thermodynamics.

items.q: The statement “a characteristic whose magnitude does not depend on how much material is present” describes which of the following?
o: Boundary
Surroundings
System
Intensive property
items.s: Intensive property is a characteristic whose magnitude does not depend on how much material is present.

items.q: Relative volatility may be defined as
o: the space occupied by one mole of a substance at stated conditions
the ratio of net work output to the energy supplied from the hot reservoir
the ratio of the vapour pressures of two components, which measures how easily they can be separated
the ideal sequence of a gas turbine, with compression, warming at constant pressure and expansion
items.s: Relative volatility: the ratio of the vapour pressures of two components, which measures how easily they can be separated. The other options describe Thermal efficiency, Molar volume, Brayton cycle.

items.q: Which term is described by “the relation giving the slope of a phase boundary from the enthalpy and volume changes of the transition”?
o: Clapeyron equation
Joule-Thomson coefficient
Helmholtz free energy
Gibbs free energy
items.s: Clapeyron equation is the relation giving the slope of a phase boundary from the enthalpy and volume changes of the transition.

items.q: Which of the following best describes System?
o: the statement that the total pressure of a gaseous mixture equals the sum of the pressures of its components
an expression of state that adds corrections for molecular attraction and for the finite size of molecules
the ratio of the actual volume of a gas to the volume it would occupy if it behaved perfectly
the defined quantity of matter or region of space chosen for study
items.s: System: the defined quantity of matter or region of space chosen for study. The other options describe Dalton's law, Van der Waals equation, Compressibility factor.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ratio of product activities to reactant activities, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient”?
o: Van't Hoff equation
Equilibrium constant
Heat of combustion
Extent of reaction
items.s: Equilibrium constant is the ratio of product activities to reactant activities, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Steady state.
o: a device that lifts thermal energy from a cooler region to a warmer one using work input
the statement that the total pressure of a gaseous mixture equals the sum of the pressures of its components
the energy required to raise the temperature of a given amount of material by one kelvin
a condition in which every property at a fixed point stays unchanged with time
items.s: Steady state: a condition in which every property at a fixed point stays unchanged with time. The other options describe Heat capacity, Dalton's law, Heat pump.

items.q: Path function may be defined as
o: the condition at which the first bubble of vapour forms in a liquid mixture being warmed
the space occupied by one mole of a substance at stated conditions
a characteristic whose magnitude does not depend on how much material is present
a quantity whose value depends on the sequence of steps taken between two conditions
items.s: Path function: a quantity whose value depends on the sequence of steps taken between two conditions. The other options describe Molar volume, Bubble point, Intensive property.

items.q: Which term is described by “an absolute basis for measuring hotness defined by the efficiency of reversible engines, independent of any working fluid”?
o: Second law of thermodynamics
Entropy generation
Thermodynamic temperature scale
Thermal efficiency
items.s: Thermodynamic temperature scale is an absolute basis for measuring hotness defined by the efficiency of reversible engines, independent of any working fluid.

items.q: Which term is described by “the statement that the partial pressure of a dissolved gas is proportional to its mole fraction in the liquid”?
o: Henry's law
Lever rule
Raoult's law
Dew point
items.s: Henry's law is the statement that the partial pressure of a dissolved gas is proportional to its mole fraction in the liquid.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Virial coefficient?
o: a parameter appearing in the power series expansion of the compressibility of a gas in density
everything outside the chosen enclosure that can exchange mass or energy with it
the statement that the partial pressure of a component equals its liquid mole fraction times its vapour pressure
the sum of all the molecular kinetic and potential energies inside a body
items.s: Virial coefficient: a parameter appearing in the power series expansion of the compressibility of a gas in density. The other options describe Raoult's law, Internal energy, Surroundings.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Entropy?
o: a characteristic whose magnitude grows in proportion to the amount of material present
the principle that the total dispersal of energy in an isolated arrangement can never decrease
the ratio of product activities to reactant activities, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient
a measure of the dispersal of energy in a body of matter, which always rises for an isolated change
items.s: Entropy: a measure of the dispersal of energy in a body of matter, which always rises for an isolated change. The other options describe Equilibrium constant, Extensive property, Second law of thermodynamics.

items.q: Intensive property may be defined as
o: the ratio of the work of an ideal reversible machine to the work of the real machine for the same inlet condition
a potential whose decrease at constant temperature and pressure equals the maximum non expansion work
a device that lifts thermal energy from a cooler region to a warmer one using work input
a characteristic whose magnitude does not depend on how much material is present
items.s: Intensive property: a characteristic whose magnitude does not depend on how much material is present. The other options describe Isentropic efficiency, Gibbs free energy, Heat pump.

items.q: Chemical potential may be defined as
o: the most efficient reversible sequence of four steps operating between two constant thermal reservoirs
the space occupied by one mole of a substance at stated conditions
everything outside the chosen enclosure that can exchange mass or energy with it
the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions
items.s: Chemical potential: the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions. The other options describe Molar volume, Carnot cycle, Surroundings.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ideal sequence of a gas turbine, with compression, warming at constant pressure and expansion”?
o: Regeneration
Throttling
Brayton cycle
Compressor
items.s: Brayton cycle is the ideal sequence of a gas turbine, with compression, warming at constant pressure and expansion.

items.q: The statement “an absolute basis for measuring hotness defined by the efficiency of reversible engines, independent of any working fluid” describes which of the following?
o: Thermodynamic temperature scale
Carnot cycle
Entropy
Entropy generation
items.s: Thermodynamic temperature scale is an absolute basis for measuring hotness defined by the efficiency of reversible engines, independent of any working fluid.

items.q: The statement “the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions” describes which of the following?
o: Gibbs free energy
Clapeyron equation
Joule-Thomson coefficient
Chemical potential
items.s: Chemical potential is the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions.

items.q: Azeotrope may be defined as
o: the relation that predicts how the equilibrium quotient varies with temperature from the enthalpy change
the potential whose decrease at constant temperature and volume gives the maximum work of a change
a mixture that boils at constant composition because its vapour has the same composition as its liquid
a quantity whose value depends on the sequence of steps taken between two conditions
items.s: Azeotrope: a mixture that boils at constant composition because its vapour has the same composition as its liquid. The other options describe Helmholtz free energy, Van't Hoff equation, Path function.

items.q: Which term is described by “the principle that the total dispersal of energy in an isolated arrangement can never decrease”?
o: Thermodynamic temperature scale
Heat pump
Second law of thermodynamics
Coefficient of performance
items.s: Second law of thermodynamics is the principle that the total dispersal of energy in an isolated arrangement can never decrease.

items.q: The statement “a measure of the dispersal of energy in a body of matter, which always rises for an isolated change” describes which of the following?
o: Entropy
Thermal efficiency
Heat pump
Thermodynamic temperature scale
items.s: Entropy is a measure of the dispersal of energy in a body of matter, which always rises for an isolated change.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Phase rule?
o: the ratio of net work output to the energy supplied from the hot reservoir
the ideal sequence of a gas turbine, with compression, warming at constant pressure and expansion
the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions
the statement that the number of independent variables equals the components minus the forms present plus two
items.s: Phase rule: the statement that the number of independent variables equals the components minus the forms present plus two. The other options describe Chemical potential, Brayton cycle, Thermal efficiency.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Reduced temperature?
o: the prevailing absolute thermal level divided by the corresponding value at the critical condition
a corrected pressure that replaces the true pressure so that equilibrium equations keep their simple ideal form
the defined quantity of matter or region of space chosen for study
the recovery of thermal energy from a hot stream to warm an incoming stream in the same plant
items.s: Reduced temperature: the prevailing absolute thermal level divided by the corresponding value at the critical condition. The other options describe Regeneration, System, Fugacity.

items.q: The statement “the number of moles by which a chemical change has advanced, scaled to its stoichiometric coefficients” describes which of the following?
o: Standard heat of reaction
Adiabatic flame temperature
Extent of reaction
Heat of combustion
items.s: Extent of reaction is the number of moles by which a chemical change has advanced, scaled to its stoichiometric coefficients.

items.q: Which term is described by “the number of moles by which a chemical change has advanced, scaled to its stoichiometric coefficients”?
o: Van't Hoff equation
Hess's law
Extent of reaction
Adiabatic flame temperature
items.s: Extent of reaction is the number of moles by which a chemical change has advanced, scaled to its stoichiometric coefficients.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Critical point.
o: the sum of all the molecular kinetic and potential energies inside a body
an expression of state that adds corrections for molecular attraction and for the finite size of molecules
the condition at which the liquid and vapour phases of a substance become indistinguishable
the proportionality factor in the equation of state for a gas, equal to 8.314 J per mole kelvin
items.s: Critical point: the condition at which the liquid and vapour phases of a substance become indistinguishable. The other options describe Universal gas constant, Internal energy, Van der Waals equation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions”?
o: Chemical potential
Clapeyron equation
Activity
Helmholtz free energy
items.s: Chemical potential is the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions.

items.q: Which term is described by “the force per unit area at which a vapour is in equilibrium with its liquid at a given temperature”?
o: Virial coefficient
Superheated vapour
Saturation pressure
Compressed liquid
items.s: Saturation pressure is the force per unit area at which a vapour is in equilibrium with its liquid at a given temperature.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Ideal gas law?
o: the condition at which the first drop of liquid forms in a vapour mixture being cooled
the potential whose decrease at constant temperature and volume gives the maximum work of a change
the effective concentration of a component in a non ideal mixture, referred to a chosen standard condition
the equation relating pressure, volume, temperature and amount for a gas of non interacting point molecules
items.s: Ideal gas law: the equation relating pressure, volume, temperature and amount for a gas of non interacting point molecules. The other options describe Activity, Dew point, Helmholtz free energy.

items.q: Which term is described by “a mixture that boils at constant composition because its vapour has the same composition as its liquid”?
o: Lever rule
Raoult's law
Azeotrope
Dew point
items.s: Azeotrope is a mixture that boils at constant composition because its vapour has the same composition as its liquid.

items.q: Reheat may be defined as
o: the return of partly expanded steam or gas to a heater before it is expanded further
the ideal sequence used for steam power plants, with two constant pressure and two isentropic steps
a quantity whose value depends on the sequence of steps taken between two conditions
an arrangement that allows both mass and energy to cross its enclosure
items.s: Reheat: the return of partly expanded steam or gas to a heater before it is expanded further. The other options describe Rankine cycle, Open system, Path function.

items.q: Gibbs free energy may be defined as
o: the defined quantity of matter or region of space chosen for study
the sum of the internal energy of a body and the product of its pressure and volume
a potential whose decrease at constant temperature and pressure equals the maximum non expansion work
everything outside the chosen enclosure that can exchange mass or energy with it
items.s: Gibbs free energy: a potential whose decrease at constant temperature and pressure equals the maximum non expansion work. The other options describe System, Surroundings, Enthalpy.

items.q: Molar volume may be defined as
o: the space occupied by one mole of a substance at stated conditions
the irreversible production of dispersal within a real change, always positive
the thermal level at which a gas neither warms nor cools when it is throttled
the condition at which the first drop of liquid forms in a vapour mixture being cooled
items.s: Molar volume: the space occupied by one mole of a substance at stated conditions. The other options describe Entropy generation, Dew point, Inversion temperature.

items.q: The statement “the sum of the internal energy of a body and the product of its pressure and volume” describes which of the following?
o: Reversible process
Closed system
Isothermal process
Enthalpy
items.s: Enthalpy is the sum of the internal energy of a body and the product of its pressure and volume.

items.q: All of the following belong to Ideal gases EXCEPT
o: Bubble point
Universal gas constant
Compressibility factor
Ideal gas law
items.s: Every other option belongs to Ideal gases. “Bubble point” belongs to Phase equilibria, not Ideal gases.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Reversible process?
o: the thermal level at which a gas neither warms nor cools when it is throttled
the principle that the enthalpy change of a chemical change is the same whatever route is followed
an idealised change carried out so slowly that the material stays infinitesimally close to equilibrium
the enthalpy change when reactants and products are all in their defined reference states at a stated temperature
items.s: Reversible process: an idealised change carried out so slowly that the material stays infinitesimally close to equilibrium. The other options describe Hess's law, Inversion temperature, Standard heat of reaction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Lever rule?
o: a change during which no heat crosses the enclosure of the material
the relation that gives the amount of each phase from the distances of the overall composition from the phase boundaries
an arrangement that allows both mass and energy to cross its enclosure
a cooling sequence in which a fluid is compressed, condensed, throttled and evaporated
items.s: Lever rule: the relation that gives the amount of each phase from the distances of the overall composition from the phase boundaries. The other options describe Vapour compression refrigeration, Adiabatic process, Open system.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Closed system.
o: the ratio of product activities to reactant activities, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient
an arrangement across whose enclosure no mass passes although heat and work may cross
the highest thermal level reached when a fuel burns completely without any loss to the surroundings
the space occupied by one mole of a substance at stated conditions
items.s: Closed system: an arrangement across whose enclosure no mass passes although heat and work may cross. The other options describe Equilibrium constant, Adiabatic flame temperature, Molar volume.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ratio of the work of an ideal reversible machine to the work of the real machine for the same inlet condition”?
o: Throttling
Brayton cycle
Isentropic efficiency
Reheat
items.s: Isentropic efficiency is the ratio of the work of an ideal reversible machine to the work of the real machine for the same inlet condition.

items.q: Which term is described by “the ideal sequence used for steam power plants, with two constant pressure and two isentropic steps”?
o: Regeneration
Throttling
Rankine cycle
Vapour compression refrigeration
items.s: Rankine cycle is the ideal sequence used for steam power plants, with two constant pressure and two isentropic steps.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Gibbs free energy?
o: the quotient of the capacity at constant pressure and the capacity at constant volume
a change carried out while the temperature of the material is held constant
a potential whose decrease at constant temperature and pressure equals the maximum non expansion work
the proportionality factor in the equation of state for a gas, equal to 8.314 J per mole kelvin
items.s: Gibbs free energy: a potential whose decrease at constant temperature and pressure equals the maximum non expansion work. The other options describe Universal gas constant, Isothermal process, Specific heat ratio.

items.q: The statement “the ratio of the actual volume of a gas to the volume it would occupy if it behaved perfectly” describes which of the following?
o: Partial pressure
Dalton's law
Compressibility factor
Universal gas constant
items.s: Compressibility factor is the ratio of the actual volume of a gas to the volume it would occupy if it behaved perfectly.

items.q: Reduced temperature may be defined as
o: a property whose change depends only on the initial and final conditions, not on the route
the defined quantity of matter or region of space chosen for study
the prevailing absolute thermal level divided by the corresponding value at the critical condition
an absolute basis for measuring hotness defined by the efficiency of reversible engines, independent of any working fluid
items.s: Reduced temperature: the prevailing absolute thermal level divided by the corresponding value at the critical condition. The other options describe State function, Thermodynamic temperature scale, System.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Inversion temperature?
o: the thermal level at which a gas neither warms nor cools when it is throttled
the space occupied by one mole of a substance at stated conditions
the relation that predicts how the equilibrium quotient varies with temperature from the enthalpy change
the ratio of the actual volume of a gas to the volume it would occupy if it behaved perfectly
items.s: Inversion temperature: the thermal level at which a gas neither warms nor cools when it is throttled. The other options describe Compressibility factor, Van't Hoff equation, Molar volume.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Steady state?
o: a characteristic whose magnitude does not depend on how much material is present
the principle that the enthalpy change of a chemical change is the same whatever route is followed
the principle that the total dispersal of energy in an isolated arrangement can never decrease
a condition in which every property at a fixed point stays unchanged with time
items.s: Steady state: a condition in which every property at a fixed point stays unchanged with time. The other options describe Hess's law, Second law of thermodynamics, Intensive property.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Entropy generation?
o: a characteristic whose magnitude grows in proportion to the amount of material present
the irreversible production of dispersal within a real change, always positive
the statement that the number of independent variables equals the components minus the forms present plus two
the statement that the partial pressure of a component equals its liquid mole fraction times its vapour pressure
items.s: Entropy generation: the irreversible production of dispersal within a real change, always positive. The other options describe Phase rule, Extensive property, Raoult's law.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Heat capacity?

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Standard heat of reaction?
o: the enthalpy change when reactants and products are all in their defined reference states at a stated temperature
the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is made from its elements in their standard states
the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is completely burnt in oxygen
the highest thermal level reached when a fuel burns completely without any loss to the surroundings
items.s: Standard heat of reaction: the enthalpy change when reactants and products are all in their defined reference states at a stated temperature. The other options describe Heat of combustion, Heat of formation, Adiabatic flame temperature.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Regeneration.
o: the return of partly expanded steam or gas to a heater before it is expanded further
the recovery of thermal energy from a hot stream to warm an incoming stream in the same plant
the ideal sequence of a gas turbine, with compression, warming at constant pressure and expansion
the ideal sequence used for steam power plants, with two constant pressure and two isentropic steps
items.s: Regeneration: the recovery of thermal energy from a hot stream to warm an incoming stream in the same plant. The other options describe Rankine cycle, Reheat, Brayton cycle.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Henry's law.
o: the condition at which the first drop of liquid forms in a vapour mixture being cooled
the statement that the partial pressure of a dissolved gas is proportional to its mole fraction in the liquid
the statement that the partial pressure of a component equals its liquid mole fraction times its vapour pressure
the relation that gives the amount of each phase from the distances of the overall composition from the phase boundaries
items.s: Henry's law: the statement that the partial pressure of a dissolved gas is proportional to its mole fraction in the liquid. The other options describe Dew point, Lever rule, Raoult's law.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the statement that the number of independent variables equals the components minus the forms present plus two”
o: Relative volatility
Phase rule
Azeotrope
Raoult's law
items.s: Phase rule is the statement that the number of independent variables equals the components minus the forms present plus two.

items.q: The correct meaning of Reduced temperature is
o: a measure of the deviation of a molecule from simple spherical behaviour, used in corresponding states correlations
the prevailing absolute thermal level divided by the corresponding value at the critical condition
an expression of state that adds corrections for molecular attraction and for the finite size of molecules
a condensed phase held at a pressure above the value at which it would begin to boil
items.s: Reduced temperature: the prevailing absolute thermal level divided by the corresponding value at the critical condition. The other options describe Acentric factor, Van der Waals equation, Compressed liquid.

items.q: “the ratio of net work output to the energy supplied from the hot reservoir” is the definition of
o: Entropy
Second law of thermodynamics
Carnot cycle
Thermal efficiency
items.s: Thermal efficiency is the ratio of net work output to the energy supplied from the hot reservoir.

items.q: The correct meaning of Henry's law is
o: the ratio of the vapour pressures of two components, which measures how easily they can be separated
the statement that the number of independent variables equals the components minus the forms present plus two
the condition at which the first drop of liquid forms in a vapour mixture being cooled
the statement that the partial pressure of a dissolved gas is proportional to its mole fraction in the liquid
items.s: Henry's law: the statement that the partial pressure of a dissolved gas is proportional to its mole fraction in the liquid. The other options describe Relative volatility, Dew point, Phase rule.

items.q: The correct meaning of Chemical potential is
o: the effective concentration of a component in a non ideal mixture, referred to a chosen standard condition
a potential whose decrease at constant temperature and pressure equals the maximum non expansion work
the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions
the rate of change of temperature with pressure during a throttling flow at constant enthalpy
items.s: Chemical potential: the rate at which the total energy of a mixture changes as one component is added at fixed conditions. The other options describe Gibbs free energy, Joule-Thomson coefficient, Activity.

items.q: “an arrangement across whose enclosure no mass passes although heat and work may cross” is the definition of
o: Open system
Adiabatic process
Enthalpy
Closed system
items.s: Closed system is an arrangement across whose enclosure no mass passes although heat and work may cross.

items.q: Three of these relate to Second law and entropy. Which one does not?
o: Boundary
Second law of thermodynamics
Entropy
Carnot cycle
items.s: Every other option belongs to Second law and entropy. “Boundary” belongs to Basic concepts, not Second law and entropy.

items.q: Inversion temperature may be defined as
o: the effective concentration of a component in a non ideal mixture, referred to a chosen standard condition
the rate of change of temperature with pressure during a throttling flow at constant enthalpy
the thermal level at which a gas neither warms nor cools when it is throttled
the relation giving the slope of a phase boundary from the enthalpy and volume changes of the transition
items.s: Inversion temperature: the thermal level at which a gas neither warms nor cools when it is throttled. The other options describe Activity, Joule-Thomson coefficient, Clapeyron equation.

items.q: The correct meaning of Hess's law is
o: the highest thermal level reached when a fuel burns completely without any loss to the surroundings
the number of moles by which a chemical change has advanced, scaled to its stoichiometric coefficients
the relation that predicts how the equilibrium quotient varies with temperature from the enthalpy change
the principle that the enthalpy change of a chemical change is the same whatever route is followed
items.s: Hess's law: the principle that the enthalpy change of a chemical change is the same whatever route is followed. The other options describe Extent of reaction, Adiabatic flame temperature, Van't Hoff equation.

items.q: The correct meaning of Equilibrium constant is
o: the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is made from its elements in their standard states
the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is completely burnt in oxygen
the ratio of product activities to reactant activities, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient
the principle that the enthalpy change of a chemical change is the same whatever route is followed
items.s: Equilibrium constant: the ratio of product activities to reactant activities, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient. The other options describe Hess's law, Heat of combustion, Heat of formation.
